newsitem.title: UK: LME to restructure price setting procedures.
newsitem.headline: LME to restructure price setting procedures.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) is to restructure its quotations committee responsible for setting daily prices from January 1997.
In a notice to members the LME said the Board had decided this change following the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) review of the market.
This will result in the LME Secretariat now being solely responsible for setting the official prices and closing prices.
The Quotations Committee (QC) will comprise up to four members of the Secretariat, with the LME's manager of Market Operations Peter Childs the chairman.
"The Chairman of the quotations committee will have absolute discretion in determining the Official and Closing prices," the LME said.
Additionally, a pool of senior LME dealers will be available for consultation by the QC. Currently, LME prices are established by a panel of dealers, as well as the Manager of Market operations.
The new system will be introduced on Monday January 27 after a two-week trial period.
